A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ODE protocol and retain matching core sections, equations, experiments, and displays. All pages are readable. v2 ends with references; v4 additionally includes Appendices A and B.

before.justification: Sections IV–V report original model evaluations, synthetic-image comparisons, hallucination analyses, and fine-tuning outcomes, including Tables I–V.

after.justification: Sections 4–5 retain the original empirical studies, while the appendices report additional model results, attribute breakdowns, and feature analysis.

M1.justification: The graph construction, four concept-selection criteria, image generation and filtering, inquiry templates, and fine-tuning procedures are unchanged. The added appendix analyses do not introduce a new ODE component.

E1.justification: The AMBER-derived concepts, COCO2014/Internet/ODE imagery, four distributions, and existence/attribute tasks are retained. However, Figure 9 introduces a group labeled contaminated without explaining whether it represents additional data or reanalyzes existing image sources, leaving possible scenario expansion unresolved.

E2.justification: Section 4.1 and Table 6 expand the evaluated model comparison from five to eight models by adding InternVL-2.5, Qwen2-VL, and Cambrian across all four ODE distributions. The original five models remain.

E3.justification: Figure 9 adds a three-group feature comparison involving real, synthetic, and labeled contaminated images; the original Figure 4 compares only real and synthetic features. Existing metrics, 808 images, 8,786 data pairs, and 800 fine-tuning pairs per distribution remain unchanged. Construction of the additional comparison group is unspecified.

E4.justification: Tables 7–10 add systematic state, number, and action breakdowns across four distributions, enabling attribute-specific failure analysis beyond v2's aggregate attribute results. Appendix A also adds the three-group feature-separation analysis. Existing distribution, clustering, and fine-tuning analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without evaluation run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The statement about varying image-generation seeds is unchanged; the added results introduce no uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1–5 retain their numerical values. Tables 6–10 add fuller distribution results, attribute-specific scores, and results for three additional models. For example, Table 6 reports Standard existence F1 of 79.6 for Cambrian alongside the retained 70.7 for LLaVA-1.5. Figure 8 adds accuracy results, and Figure 9 adds a feature-separation finding.

T1.justification: The graph definition and four mathematical selection criteria in Equations 1–4 are unchanged. Neither version adds theorems, proofs, or substantive mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the claims that dynamic graph-based evaluation mitigates contamination risks, reveals hallucinations, and supplies useful fine-tuning data. The added experiments do not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix A newly acknowledges that Internet and synthetic images have nonidentical semantics, while also asserting that recent Internet data avoids contamination. Appendix B adds attribute-specific explanations and attributes InstructBLIP's precision–recall behavior to overfitting. The main-text interpretations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v4 adds a code-availability statement and repository pointer in the abstract, absent from v2. Existing prompts, filtering threshold, sample counts, and reliance on official model hyperparameters remain unchanged. Repository availability was not externally verified.

R1.justification: v4 adds citations for InternVL-2.5, Cambrian-1, Qwen2-VL, and VaLiD. VaLiD is cited as background rather than evaluated. ODE's positioning relative to static benchmarks and earlier dynamic evaluation methods remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 corrects grammar and terminology, including CHIAR to CHAIR and Master of Laws to LLMs, revises affiliation text and section numbering, and adds two appendix sections. The main narrative order and most prose are retained.

P2.justification: v4 adds Table 6's expanded comparison matrix, four attribute tables, Figure 8's expanded accuracy/F1 display, and Figure 9's feature plot. Table 6 partly repeats Table 1, and Figure 8 redisplays earlier F1 results. Existing main displays remain, with document-wide typography and placement changes.

improvement.justification: The broader model comparison, detailed appendix results, and code pointer improve inspectability. However, added Table 7 reports LLaVA-1.5 number F1 as 94.1 despite precision 80.2 and recall 90.3, an inconsistent combination. Appendix A also leaves Figure 9's contaminated group unexplained. These problems undermine the reliability of the added evidence, making the net quality effect uncertain.
